text_blocks.snippet: Pancreatic cancer survival rates vary significantly based on stage at diagnosis, ranging from a 44% five-year survival rate for localized cancers to a 3% rate for metastatic cancers. Overall, the five-year survival rate for all stages combined is about 13% according to the Hirshberg Foundation for Pancreatic Cancer Research. Early detection is crucial, as localized cancers have a much better prognosis than those that have spread.

list.title: Regional pancreatic cancer:

list.title: Distant or metastatic pancreatic cancer:
list.snippet: If the cancer has spread to distant organs, the five-year survival rate is typically around 3.2% according to Brown University Health.
